Each cell is the model's mean task score for the suite, 0–100, from a single run.
App (Next.js): build a working Next.js application from a written brief. Graded by automated tests that drive the running app.
Design: layout and design tasks across presentations, PDFs and documents. Graded on visual and structural checks of the produced file.
Research: open-ended research briefs producing a written report. Graded against a rubric.
Browser: compound tasks in a live web application, completed through a real browser. Scored as the share of tasks passed. Models that cannot accept screenshots are marked n/a rather than scored.
Data: data-analysis questions on fixed datasets with a verified answer key. Deterministic grading.
Coding: bug-fix tasks taken from real merged pull requests on a frozen codebase. Deterministic grading; a fix that breaks existing behaviour scores 0.
Long-Horizon: long-running work — applications extended over several turns of changing requirements, plus extended coding and optimisation tasks. Deterministic grading.
Models run at their highest supported effort setting. Where a different setting was used, it is shown in the model's expanded row.

Overall is the mean of the suites a model has a score for. Blank and n/a cells are left out, so rows with fewer scored suites are marked with *. The Weights control lets you re-weight the suites; the published Overall uses equal weights.
